slides.title: Sample deck
slides.narration: Hello everyone, and welcome. This is a short sample presentation delivered by an AI presenter. It has three slides, and its only purpose is to check that everything works end to end: the slides on screen, my voice, and your questions. Feel free to interrupt me at any time.
slides.notes: This is a smoke-test deck. If asked what the tool is: it is a small Node application that drives an HTML slide deck and speaks the narration through GPT-Live-1 in full-duplex mode.

slides.title: How it works
slides.narration:
Let me explain how this works, because the mechanics are simple but they matter. A small controller running on your machine holds the slide deck and a script. The script is a Markdown file with one section per slide, and each section contains the words I am supposed to say. When a slide is shown, the controller sends me that slide's narration, and I read it out loud at a natural pace. The controller also listens to my audio. When I stop talking for about two seconds, it assumes the slide is finished and moves on to the next one. That is the whole loop: show a slide, speak the narration, wait for silence, advance.

The interesting part is that I am listening to you the entire time. The voice model I run on is full duplex, which means it can hear and speak at the same moment, the same way a person does. If you ask a question while I am talking, I will stop, answer you briefly, and then pick up the narration where I left off. The controller notices that someone is speaking and holds the slide until the conversation has settled down again.

There are three ways to control the flow. First, you can do nothing and let the presentation run by itself. Second, you can use the keyboard: the right arrow jumps to the next slide immediately, the left arrow goes back, and the space bar pauses and resumes. Third, you can click the small navigation buttons that belong to the deck itself; the controller watches the deck and follows along, so the narration always matches what is on screen.

A few practical notes. The narration for a slide can be long; the controller splits it into parts behind the scenes and sends them to me one after another, so you can write as much as you like. Background material for questions goes into a separate context file, which I can use to answer but will not recite. And because the session is billed by the minute, the controller closes it as soon as the last slide is done or when you close the browser tab. That is all there is to it: a script, a deck, a voice, and a listener. Everything else is just plumbing to make those four things stay in step with each other, slide after slide, for as long as the presentation runs. Which brings us to the last slide, where I will show you the keys you can use.

slides.title: Keys
slides.narration: Finally, the keyboard. Space pauses and resumes me. The right and left arrows move between slides. M mutes the microphone if you need a private word with someone in the room. And Escape ends the session, which also stops the billing clock. That is the end of the sample. Thank you for listening.
